title: Derinkuyu vs Kaymaklı Underground City: Which Should You Visit?
seoTitle: Derinkuyu vs Kaymaklı Underground City: Which to Visit?
metaDescription: Compare Derinkuyu vs Kaymaklı Underground City: depth, claustrophobia, knee strain, 2026 €13 tickets, visit times, and how to pair with Ihlara Valley.
quickAnswer: Choose [Derinkuyu Underground City](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?sectionId=DKY01&distId=DKY) for maximum vertical drama—eight open levels descending 85 meters—or [Kaymaklı Underground City](https://visitcappadocia.net/en/travel-guide/derinkuyu-vs-kaymakli-comparison) for wider horizontal chambers, four open levels, and a shorter 25 km drive from Göreme. Both cost €13 in 2026, take 45–75 minutes, and pair smoothly with Ihlara Valley.

body.text: Which underground city is deeper and less claustrophobic?

Derinkuyu is far deeper—reaching 85 meters across eight public levels with a 55-meter ventilation shaft—while Kaymaklı spreads wider horizontally with four open levels. For most travelers uneasy in tight spaces, Kaymaklı feels calmer because its descent is shallower and its main living rooms are broader, though both include short stooped corridors.

Originally linked by an [8–9 km subterranean tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaymakli_underground_city), both cities sheltered thousands of residents, livestock, wine presses, and churches during regional raids. The real difference is geometry: Derinkuyu pushes you steadily downward via steep rock staircases into a vast cruciform church on the seventh floor, whereas Kaymaklı winds laterally through stables, kitchens, and copper-smelting rooms.

body.text: How much time does each take?

Allow 60 to 75 minutes inside Derinkuyu and 45 to 60 minutes inside Kaymaklı, plus 15 minutes for parking and ticket scanning. If you arrive between 10:00 and 13:30 when tour coaches converge, add 20 to 30 minutes for slow-moving bottlenecks inside narrow one-way passages.

Entering at 08:00–08:45 or after 15:00 changes the entire feel of both sites. Underground airflow stays cool at roughly 13–15°C year-round, so walking without a group pressed behind your shoulders lets you actually inspect the rolling millstone doors, wine-pressing basins, and ventilation chimneys without rushing.
Are they safe for visitors with mild claustrophobia or knee issues?

Both cities are well-lit, ventilated, and structurally stable, but visitors with moderate claustrophobia, bad knees, or severe back pain should evaluate the physical demands carefully before descending. Neither site has elevators, handrails are sporadic on worn volcanic steps, and once you enter a one-way tunnel with a group behind you, turning back is awkward.
If you have mild sensitivity or joint concerns, follow these practical precautions:

items: Go at opening time (08:00–08:30): Empty tunnels eliminate the trapped feeling caused by waiting five minutes crouched behind a 30-person tour group.
Stop after Level 2 if needed: At Kaymaklı, you can inspect stables, a rolling stone door, and a kitchen on the first two floors, then exit early without descending to Level 4.
Skip Derinkuyu's lowest staircases if knees are weak: Climbing back up 85 meters of uneven, steep volcanic steps strains knees far more than Kaymaklı's four-floor loop.
Wear closed-toe grippy shoes: Dust-coated volcanic tuff becomes slick on sloped passageways; sandals and smooth leather soles slip easily.

body.text: How do you pair them with Ihlara Valley?

Pair one underground city with [Ihlara Valley](https://www.dailytoursincappadocia.com/en/blog/ihlara-valley-hiking/) and Selime Monastery in a single southern-corridor day loop from Göreme or Uçhisar. Start at Derinkuyu or Kaymaklı at 08:30, drive 45–55 minutes southwest to Ihlara's main gate (€15 entry), hike the flat 3.5–4 km riverside trail to Belisırma Village for lunch, and finish at Selime Monastery.

Ihlara's canyon stretches 14 km along the Melendiz River, but walking the full length takes 4–5 hours and leaves little time for driving back. Descending the [~360–400 stone steps](https://visitcappadocia.net/en/travel-guide/ihlara-valley-hiking-guide) into the shaded gorge, visiting frescoed churches like Ağaçaltı and Yılanlı, and letting your driver meet you in Belisırma turns a long driving day into a balanced highlight of a [3-day Cappadocia itinerary](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/3-days-in-cappadocia). For other walks closer to Göreme, check our [Cappadocia hiking trails guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/cappadocia-hiking-trails).

faq.q: Should I visit both Derinkuyu and Kaymaklı on the same trip?
faq.a: No. Both cities display the same defensive architecture—rolling stone doors, ventilation shafts, stables, wineries, and chapels. Pick one underground city and invest your extra two hours in Ihlara Valley or Soğanlı Valley instead.

faq.q: Is Derinkuyu or Kaymaklı better for children?
faq.a: Kaymaklı is generally easier for younger children because the four-level circuit is shorter and less tiring on the climb out. Children under 8 enter Ministry of Culture and Tourism sites free with passport ID.

faq.q: How cold is it inside Derinkuyu and Kaymaklı?
faq.a: Subterranean chambers stay around 13–15°C year-round, feeling refreshingly cool in July and August and slightly damp in winter. Bring a light layer in summer if you chill easily, though walking uphill warms you up fast.

faq.q: Do I need a guide inside the underground cities?
faq.a: A guide is optional—both sites have color-coded red (entry) and blue (exit) arrows—but a licensed guide brings bare rock chambers to life by explaining how ventilation shafts, trap holes, and communal kitchens actually functioned.

faq.q: Are backpacks allowed inside Derinkuyu and Kaymaklı?
faq.a: Small daypacks are allowed, but bulky backpacks scrape low ceilings and snag in narrow tunnels. Leave large bags locked in your vehicle or hotel before entering.

faq.q: What is Özkonak Underground City, and is it worth substituting?
faq.a: Özkonak sits north near Avanos rather than on the southern Ihlara highway. It is smaller and much quieter than Derinkuyu or Kaymaklı, making it a smart substitute if you have only two days and want to avoid driving south.
